title: Cauliflower and kale noodles
description: Full of fibre, this recipe makes a lovely filling meal.
ingredients: Thumb-sized piece of fresh ginger, peeled and finely grated
200g cavolo nero or kale, stalks removed and leaves finely sliced
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C/ 180°C fan/ gas mark 6. Trim any ratty leaves and the stalk from the cauliflower, wash it under cold running water, then cut the main cauliflower into florets and the leaves into chunks. Toss the florets and the leaves in 1 tablespoon vegetable oil and put in the oven to roast for 30 minutes, stirring after 15 minutes.
Put all of the ingredients for the dressing in an empty, clean jam jar and give it a good shake.
Boil a large pan of water and, once boiling, add the noodles and cook according to pack instructions (usually about 4-5 minutes). Drain well and set aside.
Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat then add the cavolo nero or kale. Cook, stirring regularly, for about 4 minutes until it is tender.
Add the cooked noodles and the cauliflower into the pan of cavolo nero or kale and pour over the dressing. Stir well to coat it with the dressing. Cook for a few minutes until everything is hot.

If serving with cashew nuts, heat a small frying pan on a medium heat (no oil) and add the cashews. Cook them for about three minutes until toasted, shaking the pan regularly so they don’t burn. If you are having eggs, poach or fry them while the noodles, cavolo nero or kale and cauliflower are finishing cooking. To serve, plate up the noodles, cauliflower and cavolo nero or kale, place an egg on top, sprinkle over some cashews and add a tablespoon of kimchi, if using.
hints: A delicious, flavoursome and lightly-spiced meal.
The noodles are the main source of carbohydrate in this dish and the values have been provided for those who have trained in insulin adjustment.

Nuts tend to be high in potassium and phosphate but you can use a small quantity of cashews in this recipe to add an extra crunch. Noodles are low in potassium allowing the addition of un-boiled vegetables to this meal.
If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, ensure you take them with this dish.
This recipe meets the criteria for a low protein meal. You may wish to add additional egg if you have higher protein requirements, but it would no longer be a low phosphate dish.
Use gluten-free noodles (eg buckwheat or rice noodles) and tamari instead of soy sauce (choose low-salt if you can).
Check that the kimchi hasn’t been made with fish or shellfish.
Exclude the egg and use maple syrup, not honey, in the dressing. Check kimchi ingredients if using.
Choose regular noodles and leave out the pricier optional extras such as kimchi and cashews.
The dressing can stored in the fridge for two days. Leftovers can be covered and refrigerated for up to two days and either eaten cold or reheated.

Many steps can be done in advance: the cauliflower can be roasted, the dressing can be made up and the cavolo nero can be prepared, ready to cook, meaning that all you need to do when you want to eat is cook the noodles, cook the cavolo nero and add in the already-cooked cauliflower and dressing to heat it all through.

title: Beef stir fry
description: This dish is high in protein so would make a suitable dinner for someone having dialysis.
ingredients: 1 very low salt or zero salt beef stock cube
250g raw basmati rice, rinsed and drained.
steps: Cut the beef into 1cm strips and place in bowl. Add the paprika and chilli powder, evenly coating the beef. Leave to marinate for 1 hour. Stir after 30 minutes and check the beef is well coated.
Add the rice to a saucepan and pour over 500ml of water. Bring to a rolling boil and reduce the heat to a gentle simmer. Cook for 12 minutes.
Cut the celery and pepper into 5 cm lengths and then into strips about 5 mm thick. Thinly slice the spring onions and set aside.
Heat the oil in a wok or large frying pan and fry the spring onions, garlic, celery and peppers for one minute before adding the steak. Continue to fry on a high heat for 3-4 minutes.
Make up the sauce by adding one stock cube to 60ml of boiling water and adding the Worcestershire sauce, honey and red wine vinegar. Add the sauce and cook until the meat is well coated.
Drain the rice and rinse with boiling water, serve immediately.
hints: Whip up this tasty, Asian inspired stir fry with tender beef. Perfect for a busy weeknight dinner or to make ahead and freeze.

The main source of carbohydrate in this dish is provided by the rice. However, the honey will also add to the carbohydrate of this meal. The carbohydrate values have been provided for those who have trained in insulin adjustment.
If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder ensure you take them with this dish.
This recipe is very high in protein which is great for people on dialysis. If you have been advised to reduce your protein intake, have a smaller portion of the beef.
Use a gluten-free stock cube and serve with rice.
The beef can be replaced with vegetarian protein such as tofu or Quorn pieces to suit a vegetarian diet.
Replace the beef with tofu or a vegan alternative, miss out the honey and use one tablespoon of golden syrup in its place.
Substitute the beef with turkey or tofu for an equally tasty but cheaper dish.

Freeze any left-over beef stir fry but we do not recommend freezing rice. To defrost, remove the lid from the container and leave in the fridge to defrost slowly. Reheat thoroughly either in your wok, frying pan or in the microwave.

title: Bean stew
ingredients: 1 low-salt vegetable stock cube made up with 300ml boiling water
400g tin of white beans (any type) rinsed and drained
2 thick slices of bread or 2 crusty rolls
steps: Put the carrots into a pan and cover with the boiling stock. Simmer for 4 minutes.
Add in the drained beans, tomato puree and mixed herbs and stir.
Reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes, then add the frozen peas and cook for 3-5 minutes more.
Serve into 2 dishes with the bread and season with black pepper. Sprinkle over the grated cheese.
hints: A wholesome, high-protein vegetarian dish that’s also low in potassium and phosphate.

The bread is the main source of carbohydrate in this main meal, however the beans will also be a source of carbohydrate. The value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.

This dish is low in potassium; if you have been advised to follow a low-potassium diet, ensure you keep to the quantities stated. This recipe is low in phosphate, however does contain some phosphate, due to the beans and cheese, therefore if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder please ensure you take them with this dish.

This dish is high in protein and therefore suitable for those receiving dialysis. If you have been advised to eat less protein then you may wish to swap the peas for sweetcorn and/or reduce the quantity of cheese to 30g.

title: Caribbean oven baked salmon with sautéed vegetables
description: A low potassium and low phosphate recipe with a spicy kick. Serve with rice to make a balanced meal.
ingredients: Handful of fresh thyme or lemon thyme
steps: Make the Caribbean green seasoning by blending together the spring onions, scotch bonnet, garlic, thyme, coriander, basil, onion and celery in a food processer. Place the salmon in a bowl and clean it with the lemon. Add 2 tablespoons of the seasoning and mix. Leave it in the fridge overnight, or for at least an hour before cooking.

Heat the oven to 190°C/ 170°C fan /gas mark 5. Place the salmon in a greased baking tin and drizzle with some oil. Cover with foil and cook for 20 minutes. Fill a large saucepan with water and bring to the boil. Prepare your vegetables by finely slicing the celery, white cabbage, peppers and carrot.

Remove the foil covering the salmon and then cook for a further 10 minutes until slightly brown. During those last 10 minutes, boil the sliced vegetables in plenty of water until slightly soft and then drain.
Sauté the boiled vegetables in 2 tablespoons of oil for 3 minutes in a frying pan, adding a little of the Caribbean seasoning for taste. Serve the salmon on a bed of the sautéed vegetables.
hints: Caribbean green seasoning is a versatile sauce or paste that is often used throughout the Caribbean islands. Marinade the fish and add to vegetables to pack in lots of flavour.

This recipe is low in carbohydrate and the values have been provided for those who have trained in insulin adjustment. To make this a more balanced meal serve with rice or a small portion of cornmeal pie.

The boneless fish used here helps to keep the phosphate low. If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder ensure you take them with this dish. Boiling the vegetables first reduces their potassium content. If you do not need a low potassium diet you can sauté the vegetables from raw. The green seasoning contains raw ingredients and is therefore higher in potassium so should only be used in small amounts.
Fish is a great low fat source of protein. Sea bream or sea bass fillets also work well with this dish as an alternative.
You could use frozen fish to reduce the cost (defrost thoroughly in the fridge before cooking).
If you add a tablespoon of cider vinegar to the green seasoning it can be made in advance and kept in the fridge for up to five days.
Add 2 scotch bonnet peppers to your Caribbean green seasoning if you like it hot!
If you have a transplant you should buy your fish pre-packaged, rather than from a fishmonger or a fish deli counter, in order to avoid any risk of bacterial contamination.

title: Chicken and pepper one pot
steps: Preheat oven to 190°C / fan 170°C / gas mark 5. Put olive oil into a flameproof casserole dish and place over a medium heat on the hob. Season chicken with black pepper and cook until sealed on each side. Transfer to a plate for later.
Add the peppers into dish and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, then add shallots, garlic and chillies. Cook for a further 5 minutes until softened. Stir in orzo and paprika.
Pour the stock over and an additional 200ml of boiling water to completely cover the orzo. Place the chicken and tomatoes on top of the orzo and bake in oven for 30 minutes.
Serve in bowls, topped with the crème fraîche and chopped parsley if desired.
hints: An easy, mid-week supper dish, suitable for all stages of kidney disease.
The orzo (pasta) is the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.

This recipe is low in potassium, when following the quantities in the ingredients, and the serving sizes. The recipe is also low in phosphate, however it does contain some phosphate, mainly provided by the chicken, so if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, you should take as directed.

This recipe is high in protein, therefore suitable for those advised to eat more protein, such as those receiving dialysis. If you have been advised to eat less protein, you may wish to reduce the chicken and add a tin of chickpeas. This would also lower the potassium and phosphate content.
This dish is best eaten freshly made.
Uncooked rice can be used in place of orzo if your supermarket doesn’t stock it.

title: Caribbean vegetable curry
description: A creamy, low protein, vegetable-packed curry that’s low in salt, potassium and phosphate.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons green seasoning, or 1 tablespoon of mixed herbs
4-6 wholemeal pitta breads, roti, naan bread or chapatti
steps: Heat a large frying pan over a medium heat and add the oil. Once the oil is hot, tip in the curry powder and turmeric, mix them in the pan and then add the chopped onion, garlic and ginger. Stir and cook gently until the onion is slightly soft.
When the onion has softened, add the drained chickpeas, green beans, red pepper, celery and sweetcorn.
Add the green seasoning to the curry with 200ml of water and simmer on a low heat for 5-10 minutes. Add the yoghurt, stir and simmer again on a low heat for 1 minute.
Once the curry is ready, toast the pitta breads (or prepare the roti, naan or chapatti). Serve into four bowls with your desired bread, yogurt and chopped coriander.
hints: A quick and great value calypso curry, made in one pot for minimal washing-up!
The pitta bread, naan or chapatti is the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
This recipe is low in potassium, when following the quantities in the ingredients, and the serving sizes. Therefore, suitable for those advised to reduce potassium in their diet.

This recipe is also low in phosphate, however it does contain some phosphate, mainly provided by the chickpeas, pitta bread and yogurt, therefore if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder you should take as directed.
This recipe is low in protein, therefore suitable for those advised to eat less protein.
Use a gluten-free pitta bread, naan, or chapatti.
Use a vegan yogurt, such as soya.
Once cooked and cooled, this recipe can be stored in an airtight container in the fridge and reheated for the following day.

title: Broc-cauli cheese
description: A simple twist on cauliflower cheese, made with both cauliflower and broccoli. It provides a source of protein and is low in potassium, phosphate and salt when enjoyed in the recommended portion size.
ingredients: 1 small head of cauliflower, broken into florets
1 small head of broccoli, broken into florets
1 teaspoon English mustard (or Dijon if preferred)
steps: Cook the baguettes according to the instructions and then set aside to cool.

Preheat oven to 180°C / 160°C fan / gas mark 4. Put the cauliflower and broccoli into a pan of water and bring to the boil and cook for approximately 5 minutes until the vegetables are almost tender. Remove from the heat and drain.

Make the sauce by heating the cream cheese over a medium heat to loosen it and then whisk in the milk to fully combine into a sauce with a good grind of black pepper and the English mustard. Remove from the heat.
Arrange the cauliflower and broccoli into a baking dish and pour over the cheese sauce. Sprinkle the grated Cheddar over the top and then cook in the oven for 25 minutes until nicely golden.

While this is cooking, make the garlic butter by mixing the butter with the garlic purée and dried herbs, beat well. Halve the cooked baguettes and spread with the garlic butter. Put the two halves of baguette back together and wrap in tin foil. Add into the oven with the cauliflower cheese with 10 minutes remaining on the cooking time.
hints: A twist on a family classic
Serving sizes are based on adult portions. Here is a guide for children:

Some children do have bigger appetites than others. You child’s portion may need to be changed to fit their typical diet if you think the recommended serving sizes are too large or small. We would advise speaking with your dietitian prior to increasing the serving size if your child has struggled to manage potassium or phosphate.
The baguette is the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.
If you need to gain weight, have a growing child who needs more calories, or have a poor appetite, you can use whole milk to make the cheese sauce and add extra butter to the garlic bread.

This recipe provides a source of protein but is not high in protein. If you have been advised to eat more protein, be sure to include higher protein foods at your other meals and snacks throughout the day.
This recipe is low in potassium, when following the quantities in the ingredients, and the serving sizes. Therefore, suitable for those advised to eat less potassium.

This recipe is also low in phosphate, however it does contain some phosphate, mainly provided by the milk, and cheeses, therefore if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder you should take as directed.
Use vegan alternatives to cream cheese, milk and Cheddar.
To reduce saturated fat and increase fibre, consider using lower fat milk, lower fat cream cheese and choosing wholemeal baguettes.

This recipe has been kept as low cost as possible, however cream cheese could be replaced with a supermarket own-brand alternative, fresh garlic can be used instead of garlic purée, and the dried parsley can be omitted.
Leftovers can be stored in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheated. The cauliflower cheese can be made the day before and kept in fridge overnight, then cooked.

title: Baked cod fillet, tabouli and tomato salsa
description: A high protein meal, low in potassium, phosphate and salt. Perfect for those receiving dialysis.
ingredients: Pinch of freshly ground black pepper
Pinch of freshly ground black pepper
Pinch of freshly ground black pepper
steps: Pour boiling water over the couscous. Cover for 10-12 mins until absorbed. Mince the garlic, chop the herbs and deseed and dice the tomatoes and cucumber. Fluff with a fork and stir in olive oil, lemon juice and garlic. Stir in the tomatoes, cucumber and spring onions. Season with pepper and rest for 1 hour covered in cling film.
To prepare the herb crust for the cod, grate the cheese and combine in a bowl with the breadcrumbs and herbs. Season with pepper, then chill for 30 minutes to allow the mixture to firm up.

Preheat the oven to 200°C / 180°C / gas mark 6. When firm, roll crust mixture between 2 sheets of greaseproof paper, cut into squares large enough to cover the pieces of cod. Press it down gently so that it sticks. Brush baking sheet with olive oil and add the cod. Bake for 6-8 minutes until the cod is just cooked.

To make the salsa, chop the tomatoes and deseed and finely chop the chilli. Place in a bowl and add the herbs. Season with pepper and mix until well combined. To serve, place a piece of herb-crusted cod on each plate spoon the salsa around the cod and serve with tabouli on the side.
hints: This is a delightful fresh fish dish with a serving of tasty herby tabouli on the side.
The couscous and breadcrumbs are the main sources of carbohydrate in this main meal and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.

This dish does contain ingredients that are high in potassium and phosphate. However, the quantities have been kept to a minimum and by using the quantities listed and following the recommended serving size, the overall phosphate and potassium content of the dish remains low. If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, ensure you take them with this dish.
The fish in this recipe provides a good source of protein, ideal for those receiving dialysis.
Serve with rice, quinoa or gluten-free pasta instead of couscous. Use gluten-free breadcrumbs.
Stir a 400g tin of drained chickpeas into the tabouli and serve with the salsa.

Choose cheaper fillets of fish, frozen fillets, or fish on offer to reduce the cost. You can buy pre-packaged breadcrumbs or save money by making your own. To save money, use a teaspoon of dried mixed herbs as an alternative to the fresh herbs in the cod crust.
Fish should be eaten on the day of cooking. Tabouli and salsa can be kept in an airtight container in the fridge for up to two days.

For those with a transplant, it is best to purchase your fish pre-packaged. Good choices for mixed fresh herbs include basil, chives or parsley. Attentively, use some extra mint, coriander and dill to complement the tabouli.

title: Asian turkey wraps
description: Also good for a healthy packed lunch.
ingredients: 1 clove garlic, minced or finely chopped
100g carrot, peeled and cut into fine strips
50g chickpeas, drained and dried on kitchen paper
steps: Heat half the oil in a frying pan over a medium heat and fry onion until soft. Add in the turkey, garlic and chilli and cook until turkey is cooked through, about 10 minutes. Add in carrot and cook for a further 5 minutes. Drain the excess liquid out of the frying pan and turn off heat.
Add the soy sauce, coriander, mint and lime juice to the turkey mixture and set aside for the flavours to develop.
Heat remaining oil in a separate pan over a high heat and add chickpeas and cumin seeds. Cook until crispy; keep them moving so they don’t burn.
Warm the tortilla wraps. Divide the turkey mixture equally between the two wraps. Top with chopped spring onions, chickpeas and lettuce. Seal and roll-up wraps to serve.
hints: This is a delicious, healthy, high-protein wrap.
The wholemeal tortilla wraps are the the main source of carbohydrate in this recipe, and the value has been provided for those who have been trained in insulin adjustment.

This recipe is low in potassium, when following the quantities and serving sizes given. This is suitable for those advised to reduce potassium in their diet. The recipe is also low in phosphate, however it does contain some phosphate, mainly provided by the turkey mince and chickpeas, therefore if you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, you should take as directed.

This recipe is high in protein, therefore suitable for those advised to eat more protein, such as those receiving dialysis. If you have been advised to eat less protein, you may wish to reduce the quantity of turkey mince and top it with some extra tinned and drained chickpeas.

It could also be a quick meal on a busy day by preparing the filling in advance (cool after step 1 and store in the fridge for up to 3 days, then warm the filling and follow recipe from step 2). Also good for a healthy packed lunch.

title: Baked blueberry and elderflower cheesecake
description: Lovely for an occasional luxury treat, the subtle blueberry and elderflower flavours can be enjoyed on a low potassium diet.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C / 155°C fan / gas mark 4. Line a 23cm round spring-form tin with greaseproof paper, smoothing out the edges. Crush the digestive biscuits into fine crumbs, melt 40g of the unsalted butter and mix together. Press the crumb mix firmly into the base of the tin.
Cream the remaining 150g unsalted butter and the caster sugar together, add in the cream cheese and beat until fluffy. Stir in the cornflour.
Beat in the eggs, cream and elderflower cordial. Mix well and pour the mixture into the tin. Press the blueberries into the mix so that they are evenly distributed and just under the surface.

Bake in the oven for one hour. Allow to cool, then rest in the fridge overnight to settle. Remove from the fridge, wait 30 minutes before removing from the tin and sieve over a little icing sugar to decorate.
hints: Try this deliciously indulgent cheesecake. Make the day ahead so it’s perfect to serve for dessert when you have friends over. You can also freeze in portions for an occasional treat.

The main source of carbohydrate in this dish comes from the sugar, digestive biscuits, cornflour and cordial. The carbohydrate values have been provided for those who have trained in insulin adjustment.

Cream cheeses, tend to be lower in phosphate than hard cheeses but as this recipe uses a large quantity of cream cheese it is high in phosphate. If you have been prescribed a phosphate binder, ensure you take them with this dish.
Blueberries are a low potassium fruit that add colour and flavour to this dessert. By sticking to the recommended portion size in the recipe it keeps the overall potassium content low.
The cheese and eggs are great sources of protein, ideal if you are on dialysis but may not be suitable if you have been advised to follow a lower protein diet.

Cheesecakes are high in fat and sugar and should be kept for special occasions or as a treat. If you want to reduce the amount of sugar or fat in this recipe, you can use a low fat spread in place of the butter, choose reduced-sugar digestives (if available) or use a sugar free/no added sugar cordial.
A cheaper option is use frozen blueberries but don’t thaw them before use.

Store in an airtight container in the fridge and eat within two days. You can easily freeze this cheesecake for up to 2 months. Cover tightly and freeze in portions. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before serving.

title: Gozleme
description: Try crispy Turkish gözleme stuffed with cheese, spinach, or meat - hand-rolled flatbread cooked to golden perfection for a tasty snack or meal.
steps: Mix together the bread flour, Renastep and water in a bowl until a dough is formed, knead for 2 minutes then set aside to rest for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, add to a frying pan the onions and peppers and allow to cook until soft.
Add in the lamb mince, garlic and cumin and allow to cook until the mince has browned.
Add in the kale and allow to soften, then remove the pan from the heat and add in the mint and coriander, set aside to cool.
Cut the dough into 4 portions and roll out each portion into a thin 15cm circle.
Place a quarter of the meat mixture onto one half of each dough circle, crumble feta equally over each gozleme.
Fold over other half of dough and crimp sides until sealed.
Brush each gozleme with olive oil and squash slightly to flatten.
Heat olive oil in a pan and fry each gozleme until golden brown and crispy on each side.
Serve and enjoy!
hints: Renastep is a food for special medical purposes for the dietary management of kidney disease. Suitable from 3 years of age. Must be used under medical supervision. Renastep contains Milk (milk protein) and Fish (Tuna oil). This recipe has been specifically designed for the dietary management of kidney disease and has been analysed using Nutritics dietary analysis software. Refer to labels for allergen and other product information.

title: Rose Tea Latte
description: Enjoy this quick and easy to make rose tea latte, which you can make in less than 10 minutes. The tea contains Renastep a food for special medical purposes.
steps: Place the rose tea bag into a cup with the boiling water and allow to brew for 3-4 minutes or as per guidance the packaging. Then carefully remove the tea bag.
Warm Renastep gently in a pan on a low heat.
In a cup, mix the beetroot powder with a small amount of Renastep to make a paste, then stir in the remaining Renastep.
Pour in the rose tea and mix well.
Serve warm.
hints: Serve as an iced latte – use chilled Renastep and serve over re-useable ice plastic cubes. Red or pink food colouring can be used instead of beetroot powder. Sprinkle with cinnamon to serve.

Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision. Renastep is a ready to use feed for the dietary management of kidney disease from 3 years of age onwards. Renastep contains milk and fish. Refer to labels for allergen and other product information. This recipe has been specifically designed for the dietary management of kidney disease and has been analysed using Nutrimen dietary analysis software.

title: Carrot purée
description: Make a smooth and tasty Carrot Purée recipe, perfect for your child's first foods. Simple to prepare, supporting your weaning journey.
ingredients: 100ml of breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialized low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian)
steps: Peel 2 carrots.
Chop carrots into small pieces.
Boil carrots until soft (10-12 minutes).
Drain water and allow carrots to cool.
Add breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian).
Use a blender to whizz up to a purée consistency.
Add more milk if a thinner consistency required.
Use straight away or add in to ice cube trays.

title: Broccoli Fritters
description: A quick renal friendly snack, these broccoli fritters which contain Renastep, take just 15 minutes to make.
steps: Mix the plain flour and paprika in a bowl, set aside.
Whisk together the Renastep and egg in a jug until fully combined.
Pour the Renastep and egg mixture into the bowl with the flour and whisk well until there are no lumps remaining.
Add in the grated broccoli and mix well.
Heat the oil in a pan and spoon out 8 separate fritters and fry on both sides until golden brown.
Serve and enjoy!
hints: Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision. Renastep is a ready to use feed for the dietary management of kidney disease from 3 years of age onwards. Renastep contains Milk (Milk protein) and Fish (Tuna oil). This recipe has been specifically designed for the dietary management of kidney disease and has been analysed using Nutritics dietary analysis software. Refer to labels for allergen and other product information.

title: Potato Croquettes
description: Try this Potato Croquettes recipe which is suitable for those on a renal diet. This lovely side dish makes 3 portions and cooks in 30 minutes.
steps: Cut the potatoes into small pieces and boil them in hot water. When the potatoes are soft, drain the water. Please be careful when you do this as the water will be very hot.
If you have been advised to follow a low potassium diet, boil and drain the potatoes again to reduce the potassium content further.
Once drained, add the butter and yolk to the potatoes and, using a potato masher, mash until creamy. You can add pepper to taste.
Cover the mash and leave until firm and cool enough to handle.
Preheat the oven to 200°C/180 Fan/Gas 6.
Shape the mashed potato into 6 croquettes, weighing around 60g.
Put the flour, whole egg and breadcrumbs into three separate shallow bowls. Beat the egg.
Dip each croquette in the flour, pat off any excess, then coat in the egg before dipping in the breadcrumbs. Transfer to a baking tray.
Using spray oil, lightly spray the croquettes.
Bake for 20 minutes or until golden-brown. If preferred, the potato croquettes can be cooked in an air fryer for 12 minutes.
hints: Finely chopped spring onions and herbs can be added to the mash for extra flavour.

title: Sweet and sour tofu
description: Learn how to cook crispy tofu in a glossy sweet and sour sauce with vibrant veggies - tangy, flavorful and satisfying, a perfect plant-based dinner.
steps: Pour cornflour into a bowl and mix in the paprika, add tofu to the bowl and toss until evenly covered.
Heat half the sesame oil in a frying pan and add the tofu, cook until golden brown and crispy then remove from pan and place onto kitchen paper.
Heat the remaining oil into the pan and add in the onions and red pepper. Cook until soft.
Add in the garlic, ginger, pineapple chunks, soy sauce, honey, rice vinegar, tomato puree and cook until fragrant.
Add in water (you don’t have to use all of it) and mix until a sauce forms, add the tofu back into the mixture and coat with sauce.
Remove from heat and sprinkle with coriander, serve with rice.

title: Raspberry Panna Cotta
description: Made with Renastep, this indulgent raspberry panna cotta recipe has been created to support a renal diet. Try making this delightful dessert today.
steps: Pour the double cream into a glass mixing bowl and whisk until soft peaks are formed.
Fold in the Renastep and leave the mixture to chill in the fridge for 5 minutes.
Dissolve the jelly in boiling water. Leave to cool until almost set.
Combine the jelly and double cream/Renastep mixture using a spoon and pour into two moulds.
Leave in the fridge for 2-3 hours to set.
hints: Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision.
Renastep is a ready to use feed for the dietary management of kidney disease from 3 years of age onwards. Renastep contains milk and fish. Refer to labels for allergen and other product information.
This recipe has been specifically designed for the dietary management of kidney disease.

title: Umm Ali
description: Enjoy this kidney-friendly twist on Umm Ali – a warm, comforting dessert made with low-potassium ingredients and full of cozy, satisfying flavor.
ingredients: 55g Palmier biscuits or frozen puff pastry
steps: Pre-heat the oven to 200˚C/ 180˚C fan /Gas Mark 6.
If using pastry, unroll and place flat on baking sheet. Bake for 15 minutes in the preheated oven, or until puffed and golden. Once cooked, allow to cool and then break into small pieces.
Place ¾ of the broken pastry/palmier biscuits in the oven proof ramekin in layers. Sprinkle the coconut over the pastry.
. Pour the Renastep into a pan and stir in the cinnamon and vanilla. Heat gently but don’t boil.
Pour the heated mixture over the pastry/palmier biscuits in the oven proof dish.
Use the final ¼ palmier biscuits or pastry to top the surface of the dish.
Place dish in the oven and bake for 10 minutes, until the liquid bubbles at the edges.
Serve warm, topped with a small portion of almonds, pistachios and raisins if permitted.
hints: Add a spoon of whipped cream on top to serve.

Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision. Renastep is a ready to use feed for the dietary management of kidney disease from 3 years of age onwards. Renastep contains milk and fish. This recipe has been specifically designed for the dietary management of kidney disease and has been analysed using Nutrimen dietary analysis software. Refer to labels for allergen and other product information.

title: Baba Ganoush
description: Make this simple kidney-friendly Baba Ganoush recipe in just 20 minutes. Perfect as a dipping snack with bread or raw vegetables
steps: Preheat an oven to 220°C/435°F/Gas mark 7
Place the halved aubergine flesh side down on a roasting tin and drizzle with ½ the oil. Cook for 15 -20 minutes or until the skin has charred.
Peel the charred skin from the aubergine and place the flesh into a bowl and allow to cool.
Once cooled, squeeze most of the water from the aubergine and discard.
Put the cooked aubergine into a food processor and add all the other ingredients.
Blend until smooth, serve and enjoy!

title: Creamy Pesto Pasta
description: If you're looking for a quick recipe to make with Renastep for a filling meal, this creamy pesto pasta is ideal.
steps: Heat a pan of water until boiling and add in the pasta, boil for 5 minutes.
Add the broccoli to the pan and cook for a further 5 minutes, drain and set aside.
In a pan, add the pesto and allow to warm. Gradually add the Renastep, ensuring not to boil the mixture.
Once combined, add the pasta and broccoli back to the pan and stir until fully coated.
Serve, sprinkle over the parmesan and enjoy!
hints: Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Maida Peda
steps: Put ghee and refined flour in a broad non-stick pan, mix well and cook on a medium flame till light brown for 3 to 4 minutes, while stirring continuously. Add milk to bind the mixture together.
Transfer the mixture into a large plate, cool for at least 10 minutes.
Add the sugar and cardamom powder and mix gently with your hands. The mixture should bind like a dough.
Rest for 10 minutes.
Divide the mixture into 2 portions.
Roll each portion into a ball and then flatten it slightly in between your palms. Form a depression in the centre, put one strand of saffron (dipped in milk) on top of peda for better presentation.
Serve the peda or store in an air-tight container and refrigerate it till serving.
hints: Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Layali Lubnnan
description: Enjoy cooking this easy to make Layali Lubnan (Semolina Pudding) recipe which is suitable for those on a renal diet. Delicious and kidney-friendly!
ingredients: ½- 1 tsp orange blossom water (to taste)
steps: Mix the Renastep, water, semolina and sugar well in a pan and gently warm on a low to medium heat stirring continuously and scraping the bottom to stop the semolina sticking to the pan.
Once the mixture starts to simmer, lower the heat to minimum, add the ground mastika and continue stirring.
When the mixture starts to thicken, remove from the heat, add the rose water and orange blossom water and stir well.
Pour the pudding into a bowl and leave to cool for about 40 minutes.
Once the pudding has rested and cooled, place in the fridge for 5-10 minutes to chill.
Whip the cream to form soft peaks.
Serve with whipped cream and finely chopped pistachios if permitted.
hints: Pour permitted syrup or honey over to serve.

title: Idli Sambhar
description: This easy Idli Sambhar recipe with steamed idli and vegetable samba creates a balanced, low-sodium meal. Cook in 45 minutes.
ingredients: 20g red gram, soaked water, as needed
steps: For the sambhar
Heat oil in a pressure cooker and add onions, sauté well.
For the sambhar
Add in the radish, carrot, brinjal and bottle gourd. Stir fry for 2 minutes.
For the sambhar
Add soaked red gram with water, mix well and add the tamarind pulp.
For the sambhar
Boil for 10-15 minutes.
For the sambhar
Heat oil in a pan and add mustard seeds, chilli flakes, and a few curry leaves. This process is known as tempering.
For the sambhar
Pour oil mixture over the sambar, serve immediately.
For the idli
Rinse rice and black gram separately, 2–3 times and then soak both in water for 6 hours.
For the idli
Drain black gram and rice, grind to a smooth, fluffy batter with little water.
For the idli
Mix both batters in a large bowl. The consistency should be thick but pourable.
For the idli
Cover and keep the batter in a warm place for 8–12 hours (overnight). The batter should rise and look airy with tiny bubbles.
For the idli
Grease idli moulds with oil. Pour batter into each mould (¾ full), steam for 10–12 minutes on medium heat.
For the idli
Allow idlis to cool for 2–3 minutes, then gently remove with a spoon. Serve hot with sambar.

title: Aubergine and chickpea soup
description: Try our renal-friendly Aubergine and Chickpea Soup recipe. Enjoy a delicious and nutritious meal that aligns with the requirements of the renal diet. Cook it today!
steps: Heat the oil in a pan over a medium heat.
Add the aubergine, onion and garlic to the pan and sauté for 5 minutes or until soft.
Add the cumin, turmeric and chickpeas to the pan and stir.
Pour the Renastep and water into the pan, stir well and allow to warm gently.
Simmer for about 15-20 minutes, until the aubergine is fully cooked and soft.
Using a hand blender, blend the soup to the desired consistency.
Serve warm in a bowl.
hints: Chickpeas could be swapped for beans or lentils if this is advised by your dietitian. Garnish with mint or caramelised onion.

Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision. Renastep is a ready to use feed for the dietary management of kidney disease from 3 years of age onwards. Renastep contains milk and fish. Refer to labels for allergen and other product information. This recipe has been specifically designed for the dietary management of kidney disease.

title: Reindeer Yule Log
description: Get into the festive spirit by baking this Reindeer Yule Log recipe. It can be made in less than an hour and serves eight. Fun for all the family to enjoy!
steps: For the cake
Preheat the oven 180°C/ fan 160°C/ gas mark 6. Grease and line a Swiss roll tin with baking paper.
For the cake
Whisk the caster sugar and eggs in a large bowl (for around 5 minutes) until pale and light.
For the cake
Sift the self-raising flour and cocoa powder together into the mixture.
For the cake
Gently combine with a spatula (it is important not to over-mix to keep the cake light and fluffy).
For the cake
Pour the mixture into the lined Swiss roll tin. Spread the mixture gently across the baking tray ensuring it is level.
For the cake
Bake for 10-12 minutes until firm but springy to touch and the edges of the cake are starting to shrink away from the sides of the tin.
For the cake
Meanwhile put a clean tea towel on your work surface.
For the cake
Remove the sponge from the oven and turn it out onto the tea towel whilst it is still warm. Carefully peel away the baking paper from the bottom of the sponge.
For the cake
Roll the sponge up from the short end, using the tea towel underneath to help. Leave the sponge to cool.
For the buttercream
Add the softened butter and icing sugar to a large mixing bowl and whisk until smooth, light and fluffy
For the buttercream
Add in the melted Vitabite and semi-skimmed milk. Whisk until smooth.
Assembly
Unroll the sponge, spread a thin layer of buttercream and carefully roll up tightly again
Assembly
Cover the sponge with the remaining buttercream.
For the decoration

Melt the Vitabite and pour ¾ onto baking paper, smooth to create a disc that will fit the end of the Yule log. With the remaining Vitabite, pour onto the parchment in the shape of 2 antlers (connecting the face and antlers together).
For the decoration
While the Vitabite is still soft add on 2 edible eyes and 1/2 glace cherry for the reindeer's shiny nose! Leave to set.
For the decoration
Once set, add the reindeer's face onto the end of your Yule log and decorate the body with permitted sprinkles
hints: Nutritional analysis excludes sprinkles, edible eyes and 1/2 glace cherry
Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Creamy Chicken
description: This creamy chicken recipes uses Renastep to create a two portions of this simple to make, delicious main meal which takes 35 minutes to cook
ingredients: ½ white onion, peeled and chopped
1 chicken breast fillets (approx. 150g), cut into 2.5cm/1in pieces
steps: Heat the sunflower oil in a large frying pan over a medium heat and cook the onion and green and orange peppers for a few minutes until soft.
Add the chicken to the pan and brown off.
Add the basil and tarragon and stir.
Cover and simmer for about 10 minutes
Add the Renastep to the pan and simmer for approx. 5-10 minutes.
Whilst the creamy chicken is cooking, prepare the rice. For microwave or boiled rice follow the manufacturer’s instructions.
When the rice is ready, remove the creamy chicken from the heat and serve with a portion of rice.
hints: Add ½ tsp turmeric to the water whilst cooking the rice. This will make the rice a lovely yellow colour.

title: Hot Cross Buns
description: Make this traditional Easter treat with this delicious hot cross buns recipe, which is perfect for the dietary management of kidney disease.
ingredients: 250 g Plain flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C / 170°C Fan / Gas Mark 5.
In a large mixing bowl, add the flour, brown sugar, cinnamon, mixed spice, 30g of butter and yeast. Rub with your fingertips until a sandy texture is formed.
Mix the orange zest and cranberries into the flour mixture.
Warm the Renastep and remaining butter in a small saucepan (do not boil)
Pour the Renastep into the flour mixture, add the eggs and combine until the mixture forms a soft, sticky dough.

Tip the dough out onto a lightly floured work surface and knead well for 5 minutes, or until the dough is smooth and elastic. Alternatively, this can be done in a freestanding mixer using a dough hook.
Place the dough in an bowl, cover with a damp tea towel and leave to rise for about 1 hour. This is best done in a warm room.
Divide the dough into 3 equal amounts and roll with your hands into a bun type shape.
Cover loosely with a clean tea towel and let the dough rise for 15 minutes.
Once the buns have risen, put them in the oven and bake for 20-25 minutes or until golden-brown.
Remove the buns from the oven and let them cool slightly before transferring them to a cooling rack.
Meanwhile, warm the apricot jam for a few seconds in the microwave and then, using a pastry brush, brush the top of the hot cross buns with the warm jam.
Mix the icing sugar and water, then transfer to a disposable piping bag and snip off a tiny snip at the end. Pipe a cross shape on top of the bun.
hints: Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision.

Renastep is a ready to use feed for the dietary management of kidney disease from 3 years of age onwards. Renastep contains milk and fish. This recipe has been specifically designed for the dietary management of kidney disease and has been analysed using Nutrimen dietary analysis software.

title: Besan paneer cheela
description: Cook this kidney-friendly Besan Paneer Cheela recipe, a high-protein, low-sodium savoury meal suitable for kidney disease diets. 15 minute cook time!
steps: Mix gram flour and semolina with water to make thin batter of pouring consistency. Add cumin seeds and turmeric. Set aside for 10-15 minutes.
Heat oil in a pan and sautee onion for 1-2 minutes in a pan, then add ginger and paneer and cook for a further 2 minutes.
Heat a pan to a medium heat and grease it with oil. Pour the batter first and move the pan to make a circle. Once cooked on one side, flip and cook again.
Top with onion-paneer mixture and fold the cheela in half.

title: Bang bang cauliflower and asparagus
description: Cook crispy bang bang cauliflower tossed in a creamy, sauce. A flavour-packed, plant-based dish that’s quick, easy, and satisfying!
steps: Preheat the oven to 200˚C /180˚C fan / Gas Mark 6.
In a bowl combine the flour and paprika, gradually pour in the Renastep and water until a batter is formed.
Place the cauliflower florets and asparagus into the batter and coat well.
Place the panko breadcrumbs onto a plate and coat the battered florets evenly, ensuring to tap off any excess breadcrumbs.
Place all the battered vegetables onto a baking tray and bake for 25 minutes or until golden brown, making sure to turn half way through.
Meanwhile, in a small pan combine garlic, ginger, honey, siracha, lime juice, reduced salt soy sauce, sesame oil. Heat gently until just simmering then remove from the heat.
Once the vegetables have finished cooking place in a bowl and toss with the sauce until evenly coated.
Top with coriander and spring onions and serve!
hints: Renastep is a food for special medical purposes for the dietary management of kidney disease. Suitable from 3 years of age. Must be used under medical supervision. title: Pancakes
description: Cook this delicious renal friendly pancake recipe which is made with Renastep. This recipe is quick to prepare (just 10 minutes) and cook.
steps: Place the Renastep, egg, plain flour and vanilla extract into a bowl and mix thoroughly.
Heat a frying pan or crepe pan on a medium heat and add 1 tsp of sunflower oil to the pan.
When heated, pour ₁⁄₃ of the batter into the pan and cook for 1-2 minutes on each side until golden.
Repeat this step until all of the batter is used.
hints: Serve with lemon and sugar or maple syrup.

title: Apple and Cinnamon Smoothie
description: Try making this apple and cinnamon smoothie today. Embrace the season with a quick to make spiced smoothie!
steps: Place the apples and cinnamon into a blender.
Pour the Renastep into the blender with the apples and cinnamon and blend until smooth.
Serve and enjoy!
hints: Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision. title: Pear and raspberry purée
description: This quick weaning recipe is suitable for children experiencing their first solid food. Once made, you can freeze or use straight away.
steps: Peel 2 pears and chop into small pieces.
Place the pear into a saucepan, add a dash of water and boil until soft (10-12 minutes).
Add the raspberries and boil for a further 1-2 minutes.
Allow to cool and then use a blender to whizz up to a purée consistency.
Add into ice cube trays and freeze or use straight away.
hints: Mix up any combination of the fruit and vegetables above to make your own unique combination!

title: Chocolate Ice Lolly
description: Enjoy a creamy chocolate ice lolly — an easy-to-make, refreshing treat that's perfect for cooling down and satisfying your sweet cravings.
steps: Break the Vitabite into small pieces and place in a small bowl with the Renastep.
Melt in the microwave in 10 second increments until melted.
Mix together until smooth, with no lumps visible.
Pour into lolly moulds and freeze for 24 hours.
hints: Renastep and Vitabite are foods for special medical purposes and must be used under medical supervision. Renastep is for the dietary management of kidney disease and is suitable from 3 years of age onwards. Vitabite is for use in protein restricted diets and is suitable from 1 year of age onwards. title: Low tomato Bolognese sauce
description: If you love Italian food, but need to reduce your phosphate levels, try cooking this Bolognese sauce which has been created for those on a renal diet.
ingredients: 1 reduced salt chicken or beef stock cube with 200ml water
steps: Heat the oil in a pan and fry the onions, carrots and celery for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and fry for a further minute.
Add the mince to the pan and brown, breaking it up with a wooden spoon.
Add the stock, passata, basil and nutmeg and season to taste with salt and pepper.

Allow to simmer on a low heat for about an hour, using a lid that is slightly ajar to let out the steam. Serve with pasta and garlic bread. This recipe is taken from the Kidney Friendly Cookbook produced by Dietitians and Dietetic Support Workers at a Paediatric Renal Unit in the UK. Please check with your Dietitian or Doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Chicken Curry
description: Indulge in a kidney-friendly chicken curry recipe. Experience the flavors of this delicious and nutritious dish, tailored for a renal diet. Cook it today!
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, skin removed, cut into small parts
steps: Cover the uncooked chicken with lemon juice.
Mix the seasoning together and rub onto the chicken.
Allow to marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour (or preferably overnight).
Add the cup of water to the pan and simmer until fully cooked and tender.
Serve over hot rice.

title: Flan Caramel
description: Experience the creamy goodness of this kidney friendly Flan Caramel, a delicious homemade dessert which uses Renastep to create a tasty pudding.
steps: Preheat the oven to 150°C/300°F/Gas Mark 2
Warm a ramekin in the oven so it is warm when you add the caramel.

To make the caramel, put 30g sugar and 2 tbsp water into a pan. Dissolve the sugar slowly, stirring with a wooden spoon over a low heat. When dissolved, stop stirring and boil until it goes dark brown colour. Remove from the heat to ensure the caramel does not burn. Once cooled pour into the ramekin.

To make the custard, place the Renastep, double cream and vanilla extract into a saucepan and heat on low. Beat the egg yolk with a whisk in a bowl and gradually beat in the remaining sugar until combined. Stir the Renastep mixture into the egg mixture and combine with a spatula. Set aside.
Pour the custard evenly into the ramekin on top of the caramel.
Place the ramekin in a roasting tin and pour boiling water into the tin until it comes half-way up the sides of the ramekin (Bain-Marie).
Bake in the oven for 60-75 minutes.
hints: When ready to serve, turn the cups upside down.

title: Falafel and Tzatziki Dip
description: Perfect for a quick snack, this kidney-friendly recipe made with chickpeas, carrots and more, can be prepared and cooked in just 20 minutes.
steps: To a blender, add all the falafel ingredients apart from the olive oil and blend until a chunky paste.
Shape into 12 balls and set aside.
In a small bowl add yoghurt, cucumber, lemon juice, garlic and mint and mix until well combined.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and fry each falafel until golden brown on all sides.
Serve the falafel on top of the tzatziki and enjoy!
hints: Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Cheesy Leek Pasty
description: Learn how to turn Renastep into a tasty snack with this Cheesy Leek Pasty recipe which can be cooked in just 20 minutes.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F/180°C/Gas mark 4
Melt the butter in a pan and add in the chopped leeks. Allow to cook until soft and remove from the pan and set aside.
To the same pan add the cheese and Renastep, gently warm the mixture until the cheese has melted into a sauce, keep this at a low heat to avoid boiling the mixture.
Stir the leeks back through the mixture and allow to cool.
Divide the sheet of pastry in half and spoon one half of the mixture onto each half of the pastry sheet.
Fold the pastry over and crimp around the mixture to ensure it does not leak.
Place onto a baking tray and bake in the oven for 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Serve and enjoy!
hints: Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Carrot and swede purée
description: Make a delicious Carrot and Swede Purée recipe as part of your child's first foods. Easy to prepare, supporting your guide to weaning. Note: you will need a blender.
ingredients: 100ml breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian)
steps: Peel the carrot and swede chop into small pieces.
Boil the carrot and swede for 10-12 minutes, until soft.
Drain water and allow vegetables to cool.
Add 100ml breast milk, standard infant formula or a specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed (as advised by your dietitian).
Use a blender to whizz up to a purée consistency.
Add more breast milk, standard infant formula or the specialised low potassium, low phosphate feed if a thinner consistency required.
Add into ice cube trays and freeze.

title: Nut Roast
description: Perfect for a Sunday lunch this kidney-friendly Nut Roast recipe is packed with delicious vegetables and herbs. It takes 35 minutes to prepare.
steps: Add the onions, carrots, peppers, rosemary, sage, thyme, garlic, and black pepper to a roasting tin. Drizzle with sesame oil and roast for 30 minutes or until soft.
Meanwhile, in a jug, add the boiling water, balsamic vinegar, stock cube, miso paste, and lemon juice, mix well, and set aside.
Once roasted, add all the vegetables, walnuts, chestnuts, and cornflour to a blender. Blend until a coarse consistency.
Once blended, remove from the blender and pour into a bowl, gradually adding the stock to loosen the mixture

Pour the mixture into a pie dish and crinkle each sheet of filo into a ball and place on top of the mixture, drizzle generously with olive oil, continue this process until all sheets of filo are used.
Bake for 25 minutes or until golden brown.
Cut to portions and serve.
hints: Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.

title: Strawberry Smoothie
description: Make this refreshing strawberry smoothie recipe, which has been created for those on a renal diet. This drink takes just 5 minutes to prepare
ingredients: 2tsp Strawberry milkshake syrup (your Dietitian can advise you on which options are suitable)
Few drops red food colouring, if desired
steps: Place all the ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth. Sieve to remove seeds, if desired.

title: Mocha Ice Lolly
description: Cool off with this easy Ice Mocha Lolly recipe! A delicious blend of coffee and chocolate, perfect for a refreshing treat on a hot day.
steps: Break the Vitabite into a small bowl and add the Renastep.
Microwave at 10 seconds intervals until completely melted.
Mix until combined and then add in the coffee. Then mix again.
Pour into lolly moulds and freeze for 24 hours.
hints: This recipe may not be suitable for children under the age of 12 years as it contains caffeine

title: Bean Burger
description: Try cooking our flavoursome vegetarian friendly Bean Burger recipe, which can be eaten by those on a the renal diet. This quick recipes makes 4 portions.
steps: Preparation for the Bean Burger Sauce
Wash the cucumber and grate using the large holes of a box grater. Drain off the excess liquid.
Preparation for the Bean Burger Sauce
Mix the cucumber with the Greek yogurt, garlic powder, dill, pepper and lemon juice to make the bean sauce.
Preparation for the Bean Burger Sauce
Cover and place in the refrigerator until ready to serve.
Preparation for the Bean Burger
Rinse and drain the tinned chickpeas. Chop the ends off the spring onions.
Preparation for the Bean Burger

Using a food processor, combine the chickpeas, spring onions, egg, flour, oregano and cumin. Blend and pulse until a mixture forms that holds together when pressed. The mixture will be moist. Form into 4 burgers.
Preparation for the Bean Burger

Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over a medium heat. When hot, add the burgers. Cook until golden and beginning to crisp (approximately 4-5 minutes). Flip and cook until golden brown and crisp (approximately 2-4 minutes more).
Preparation for the Bean Burger
Warm the pitta bread and cut each in half.
Preparation for the Bean Burger
Assemble your plate with the pitta half, bean burger and sauce. Add some red onion slices, shredded lettuce and sliced cucumber for the garnish.

title: Coconut fish curry
description: Try this delicious creamy Renastep coconut fish curry with tender fish, aromatic spices, and fresh herbs - rich, flavorful, and perfect with rice.
steps: Heat ½ of the vegetable oil in a pan and add the cumin seeds, coriander seeds and chilli flakes, cook until fragrant.
Add in the ginger, garlic, turmeric, onions and red peppers and cook until soft.
Remove from the heat and add to a blender, blend to a smooth paste.
Heat the remaining vegetable oil and fry the basa until golden brown and fully cooked.
Remove basa from the pan and add in all the curry paste and 1 low salt stock cube. Cook until fragrant and then add in the water and coconut milk.
Add the fish back into the pan with the chickpeas and Renastep and heat through.
Sprinkle with coriander and serve with rice!
hints: Renastep is a food for special medical purposes for the dietary management of kidney disease. Suitable from 3 years of age. Must be used under medical supervision. Renastep contains Milk (milk protein) and Fish (Tuna oil). This recipe has been specifically designed for the dietary management of kidney disease and has been analysed using Nutritics dietary analysis software. title: Cherry and Clove Smoothie
description: Enjoy a delicious cherry and clove smoothie! This flavorful blend combines sweet cherries with warm spices for a refreshing and nourishing treat.
steps: Put the cherries and cloves into a blender.
Pour the Renastep into the blender with the cherries and cloves and blend until smooth.
Serve and enjoy!
hints: Renastep is a Food for Special Medical Purposes and must be used under medical supervision. Renastep is a ready to use feed for the dietary management of kidney disease from 3 years of age onwards. Renastep contains milk and fish. Refer to labels for allergen and other product information. title: Basboosa
description: This golden, syrup-soaked Basboosa made with semolina, coconut, and almonds makes a delicious kidney-friendly dessert and cook in 40 minutes.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F/180°C/Gas mark 4
Mix together the semolina, sugar, baking powder, yoghurt, coconut flakes, butter, and tahini in a bowl until well combined.
Pour into a lined baking tin and flatten until level. Cut into 12 squares and press 1 almond into each square.
Bake for 30 minutes or until the cake is golden brown.
While the cake is baking, place the sugar, water, and lemon juice into a pan and dissolve the sugar. Once the mixture begins to boil, remove from the heat and set aside.
When fully cooked, remove the cake from the oven. Immediately pour over the sugar syrup and allow to cool.
Once cooled serve and enjoy!
hints: Always check with your dietitian or doctor that this recipe is suitable for you.
